recommendations.titleTemplate: Add concrete statistics
recommendations.claim: Statistics addition is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for visibility in generative-engine responses.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Statistics Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
recommendations.notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall. Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+33.9%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Cite {prevYear}/{currentYear} statistics
recommendations.claim: Generative engines preferentially cite content with recent dated statistics, treating recency markers as a freshness signal independent of the page's own publish date.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Frase, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located that publishes the specific freshness-citation correlation.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed as '83% of commercial AI citations come from sources updated in past 12 months' — that figure is widely repeated in industry blog posts but not traceable to a primary source we can cite. Queue for internal benchmark: re-audit a sample of URLs after their statistics are updated to current-year values and measure citation-count delta.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add expert quotes with named attribution
recommendations.claim: Quotation addition (named-attribution direct quotes from credible sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Quotation Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
recommendations.notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall (best-method best-metric, not per-method). Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+32%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add 2-5 outbound links to authoritative sources
recommendations.claim: Adding outbound citations to credible sources (Cite Sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility, with effect size dependent on the page's current SERP position.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Cite Sources is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1); §4.2 / Table 3 reports the effect is strongly conditioned on SERP position.
recommendations.notes: Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall (best-method best-metric, not per-method). Instead of a single per-method lift, the paper reports SERP-position-conditioned effects for Cite Sources specifically (e.g. +115.1% visibility for rank-5 sites, -30.3% for rank-1 sites). Per-method number previously displayed (e.g. '+30.3%') misread the paper's negative finding for top-ranked sites as a positive lift and has been removed. SERP-conditioned lift is captured as a methodology note for a future product feature; not surfaced as a recommendation lift figure.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Lead with a 40-60 word direct answer
recommendations.claim: Generative engines extract opening statements far more often than buried conclusions, making the first paragraph the highest-leverage location for a direct definitional answer.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, Search Engine Land); aligns with classical featured-snippet optimization literature.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add 40-60 word answer capsules after each H2
recommendations.claim: Self-contained 40-60 word answer blocks placed immediately after each H2 are among the most extractable patterns for AI engines, which often lift them verbatim as citation snippets.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, agency case studies); no controlled study located.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed as '+35-40% extraction rate' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: A/B test answer-capsule presence against citation-count on our audited corpus.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add a TL;DR or key takeaways section
recommendations.claim: Summary sections at the top of long-form content are among the most extractable patterns for AI engines, which frequently use them as citation openings and for generating quick answers to user queries.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, HubSpot, Search Engine Land); observed in high-citation content across ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Use relevant fan-out questions as headings
recommendations.claim: Headings that match relevant fan-out questions can make a page easier to retrieve for the related searches AI systems use when building an answer.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: match headings and content to relevant fan-out questions, starting with topics the page already ranks for.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Cover the most relevant fan-out questions
recommendations.claim: Expanding an existing page around tightly related fan-out questions can improve coverage of the searches AI systems use to research a topic. Generic FAQ volume is not the goal.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: use People Also Ask and fan-out research, update relevant existing pages first, and avoid creating a separate page for every question.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed as '+40% citation likelihood.' That figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. The recommendation now focuses on relevant query coverage instead of a fixed FAQ count.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add structured lists or comparison tables
recommendations.claim: Structured lists, step-by-steps, and comparison tables are heavily favored by AI extractors over dense paragraph prose.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with featured-snippet extraction patterns documented across SEO literature.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add a comparison table (pricing, features, or alternatives)
recommendations.claim: Agentic search workflows (OpenAI Operator, Perplexity Comet) browse and compare; pages with machine-readable comparison tables are pulled into agent workflows more often than prose-only pages.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner observation 2025-2026 (early agentic-search era); no controlled study yet.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Break up long paragraphs
recommendations.claim: Paragraphs over ~120 words are skipped more often by AI extractors than paragraphs of 3-5 sentences.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with classical readability + featured-snippet guidance.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Expand topical coverage
recommendations.claim: Comprehensive sources covering related questions, edge cases, and follow-ups are preferred by AI engines over thin pages.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with topical-authority SEO literature.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add original research, survey data, or proprietary statistics
recommendations.claim: Content citing original first-party data — brand surveys, internal analyses, customer case studies — is preferentially cited by AI engines because it is a unique source they cannot find elsewhere.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Frase, HubSpot); aligns with GEO paper finding that Statistics Addition is a top-performing method when data is unique and attributed.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Refresh stale content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
recommendations.claim: Content older than 24 months earns substantially fewer citations than content updated within the past 12 months. Substantive revisions are detected; cosmetic date bumps are not.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed as '3.2x citation lift moving from >24mo to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: we have an audit corpus and can re-audit a sample of URLs after their content is refreshed and measure the citation-count delta.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Refresh aging content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
recommendations.claim: Content past the 12-month freshness threshold loses citation share, especially on Perplexity and Google AI Overviews.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed as 'up to 3.2x citation lift returning to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Same internal-benchmark queue as content-stale-24mo.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add a visible "Last Updated" date and current-year markers
recommendations.claim: Perplexity and Google AI Overviews aggressively deprioritize content with no visible publish date or recent-year reference.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; widely observed but not formally measured.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add a machine-readable publish date
recommendations.claim: Year mentions in body copy are weaker than structured datetime metadata; <time> tags and article:published_time meta let AI engines verify recency unambiguously.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with schema.org best practices and Google's guidance on dated content.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Name "{brandName}" in the first 200 words
recommendations.claim: AI engines match entities by literal name; replacing pronouns and "the platform" with the brand name in opening sections improves entity matching.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with entity-disambiguation literature.

recommendations.titleTemplate: State your brand facts plainly
recommendations.claim: A consistent, factual description of the company helps people and AI systems identify what the business is, who it serves, the problem it solves, and its area of specialization.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with entity clarity and information-retrieval best practices.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add a named-author byline with credentials
recommendations.claim: Visible author credibility is part of the 2026 baseline for content cited across major AI engines; Claude in particular weights author credentials heavily.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (HubSpot, Search Engine Land); aligns with Google's E-E-A-T guidance.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Trim marketing filler
recommendations.claim: Generic filler phrases ("In today's fast-paced world…", "It's important to note…") dilute information density and contribute no extractable claims.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with general writing-quality best practices.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Reduce repeated-keyword density
recommendations.claim: Traditional keyword-stuffing is actively harmful in generative-engine contexts; AI models penalize obviously over-optimized prose.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Keyword Stuffing is identified as a non-performing optimization method (§4, Table 1).
recommendations.notes: The paper categorizes Keyword Stuffing in a section titled 'Non-Performing Generative Engine Optimization methods' and reports it scores below the unoptimized baseline across both metrics (Table 1: ~17.8 vs 19.5 baseline on Position-Adjusted Word Count). On Perplexity specifically, §4.4 states it 'performs 10% worse than the baseline.' We frame the recommendation as a negative-signal removal rather than a positive-lift intervention.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add Article JSON-LD schema
recommendations.claim: Article JSON-LD with author, datePublished, and dateModified enables richer AI extraction and unambiguous metadata interpretation.
recommendations.sourceCitation: schema.org Article specification + practitioner consensus on AI-engine schema parsing.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add FAQPage JSON-LD schema
recommendations.claim: Wrapping Q/A pairs in FAQPage JSON-LD remains widely cited as a high-ROI structured-data type for AI citations.
recommendations.sourceCitation: schema.org FAQPage specification + practitioner consensus.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add HowTo JSON-LD schema for step-by-step sections
recommendations.claim: Procedural content with HowTo JSON-LD enables richer AI extraction and is specifically eligible for distinct step-level rich results in Google AI Overviews on instructional queries.
recommendations.sourceCitation: schema.org HowTo specification + Google Rich Results documentation + practitioner consensus on AI-engine schema parsing.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Add Organization JSON-LD schema
recommendations.claim: Organization JSON-LD with sameAs links to social profiles, Wikipedia, and Crunchbase anchors brand identity in the AI knowledge graph.
recommendations.sourceCitation: schema.org Organization specification + practitioner consensus on entity-disambiguation via sameAs.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Optionally publish an llms.txt file
recommendations.claim: Server-log studies through 2026 show major AI crawlers almost never request llms.txt, and no major engine has committed to reading it. It is cheap and harmless to publish, but it is not a citation lever. Prioritize crawler access, snippet permissions, and content structure first.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Crawler-log analyses (Ahrefs, server-log studies) 2026: the overwhelming majority of published llms.txt files receive zero AI-bot requests; Google has stated it does not use the file.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Unblock AI search and fetch crawlers
recommendations.claim: If an engine's search indexer or user-request fetcher is blocked in robots.txt, citation in that engine is impossible regardless of content quality. Blocking training-only bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, meta-externalagent) is a separate IP decision that does not affect citations.
recommendations.sourceCitation: OpenAI and Anthropic crawler documentation: OAI-SearchBot/ChatGPT-User and Claude-SearchBot/Claude-User are controlled independently of the training bots; allowing them governs search citations.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Restructure passages into self-contained answers
recommendations.claim: Passages that open with a definition or direct answer and stand alone without surrounding context are extracted more reliably by AI engines than passages requiring upstream context.
recommendations.sourceCitation: AEO Improvement internal heuristic — passage-citability scoring derived from our own audit corpus. Scoring methodology documented on the methodology page; lift number pending controlled benchmark.
recommendations.notes: Previously displayed a '134-167 word optimal passage length' figure derived from classical featured-snippet length norms, not from controlled measurement against generative engines. Removed pending an internal benchmark; recommendation framed qualitatively in the meantime.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Remove nosnippet directive blocking AI extraction
recommendations.claim: The nosnippet meta tag or x-robots-tag header explicitly instructs AI engines not to use your content in answers, making citation impossible regardless of content quality. Removing it is a prerequisite for any AI visibility.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal — 'Preview Controls' ranks #2 among AI citation ranking factors (score 9.2/10) across 54 cross-referenced AI citation studies. Avoiding nosnippet is identified as the single highest-leverage technical change for AI visibility.
recommendations.notes: Score of 9.2 comes from Zyppy Signal's evidence-based AI Citation Ranking Factors framework, synthesising 54 published experiments, studies, and patents. Preview Controls (avoiding nosnippet) ranks second only to fan-out rank.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Review content hidden by data-nosnippet
recommendations.claim: The data-nosnippet attribute can keep selected page content out of supported search previews and AI surfaces. Important facts and answers should not be hidden by accident.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal, August 2026: audit noindex, nosnippet, max-snippet, and data-nosnippet controls because they can affect AI visibility.

recommendations.titleTemplate: Front-load your key answer
recommendations.claim: AI engines apply per-URL retrieval caps when extracting content. Pages that front-load their primary answer — before preambles, context-setting, or disclaimers — are more likely to have that answer extracted and cited.
recommendations.sourceCitation: Cyrus Shepard, Zyppy Signal — 'Content Placement' ranks #5 among AI citation ranking factors (score 8.8/10). Google Gemini is specifically noted to use a strict per-URL retrieval cap, making above-fold content placement critical for Gemini citations.
recommendations.notes: No controlled lift number is published for content placement in isolation. The Zyppy Signal framework assigns a practitioner-consensus score of 8.8/10 based on cross-referencing 54 published AI citation experiments; the ranking reflects expert judgment, not a measured percentage improvement attributable to placement alone.
